points.title: User interface
points.must: The part of the system the user sees and interacts with — screens, menus, buttons, forms and messages.

points.title: Navigation
points.must: How the user moves between screens: main menu / navigation bar, Back and Home buttons; a navigation structure diagram (menu → screens).

points.title: Principles of a good interface
points.must: At least four, each with a reason: consistency (same layout and button positions); clear navigation (heading, menu, Back / Home); feedback on every action; error prevention and clear error messages; simplicity; accessibility.

points.title: Suiting the interface to the users
points.must: At least two examples, e.g. large buttons and pictures for young children, big targets for a touchscreen kiosk, large text / high contrast for poor eyesight, shortcuts for experienced staff.

points.title: Input form
points.must: A screen or paper form used to enter data into the system, with labelled fields, suitable controls, validation and buttons.

points.title: Output form
points.must: A screen or printed report that presents information from the system, e.g. a receipt or a list of overdue books.

points.title: Choosing input controls
points.must: Which control for which data with the reason: drop-down list (fixed list, no spelling errors), radio buttons (one of a few), check box (yes / no), date picker (correct format), text box (free text), spinner (number in a range).

points.title: Validation checks
points.must: Validation = automatic check that data is reasonable before it is accepted (cannot prove it is true); at least four checks with an example each: presence, range, type, length, format, lookup.

points.title: Features of a good input form
points.must: At least five: title; labels; logical order; suitable controls; validation with error messages; required fields marked *; Save / Clear / Cancel buttons.

points.title: Features of a good output form
points.must: At least four: title, date and page numbers; table with column headings; sensible sort order; totals / summaries; only the needed data; print / export.

points.title: Input vs output form
points.must: A comparison: purpose (data in vs information out), main parts, validation only on input, examples.

points.title: Sketched input and output forms
points.must: A labelled sketch of an input form for a scenario (title, labelled fields, at least two different controls, an error message, named buttons) and of a report (title, date, table with headings, a total, Print / Export).

points.title: Steps to develop a prototype
points.must: List requirements → sketch navigation → design input forms (fields, controls, validation) → design output forms → build → test with users and refine.

points.title: Testing a prototype with users
points.must: Real users do realistic tasks while the developer watches; feedback is logged and sorted (change now / later / not needed); the prototype is checked against the requirements and signed off.

points.title: Prototyping tools
points.must: Paper, slides with links, a design tool such as Figma, HTML / CSS or a form designer, with the fidelity or one advantage / disadvantage of each.
